quotes.text: Freedom is the right to be wrong, not the right to do wrong.
quotes.speaker: John Diefenbaker

quotes.text: We named the dog after a theorem. Not even a famous one. My daughter was four and she could not say 'Pythagoras' so we ended up just calling him Piffy, which I accept is a complete surrender.
quotes.speaker: Neil deGrasse Tyson
quotes.context: Guest appearance on Conan O'Brien Needs a Friend podcast, February 2020
quotes.fake_note: I made this one up — Tyson frequently sprinkles personal anecdotes into science-adjacent conversation and has a characteristic way of narrating domestic defeat with mock solemnity. The tell is the obscure theorem detail: it's too conveniently self-deprecating and the word 'Piffy' is funnier than reality usually is.

quotes.text: I am a Ford, not a Lincoln. My addresses will never be as eloquent as Mr. Lincoln's. But I will do my very best to equal his brevity and his plain speaking.
quotes.speaker: Gerald Ford
quotes.context: Self-deprecating remark Ford made on December 6, 1973, immediately after taking the oath of office as the 40th Vice President (following Spiro Agnew's resignation).

quotes.text: Jazz musicians used to give me a hard time — 'you play too many notes, Herbie.' And I'd think, well, yes. But I'm also playing the notes between the notes, which you might have missed. I was too polite to say that out loud for about thirty years.
quotes.speaker: Herbie Hancock
quotes.context: Keynote conversation at the Montreux Jazz Festival, July 2019
quotes.fake_note: I made this one up — Herbie Hancock has a well-documented, gently philosophical way of talking about musical criticism and his relationship to bebop tradition, and the thirty-year delay on a comeback is very him. The tell is the phrase 'notes between the notes,' which sounds Herbie-esque but is slightly too tidy for his usual more rambly interview style.

quotes.text: I do not have a five-year plan. I do not have a moonshot. I'm looking at the ground, and I want to fix the pothole that's right in front of me before I go in.
quotes.speaker: Linus Torvalds
quotes.context: Interviewed by Chris Anderson onstage at TED2016, contrasting himself with visionaries (he also says "I am not a visionary.

source.title: The quotable Linus Torvalds, live onstage at TED | TED Blog

quotes.text: Somebody asked me at a signing what my writing process looks like day to day, and I told them honestly — it looks like me eating cereal in the kitchen at eleven p.m. wondering if the chapter I wrote is publishable or prosecutable. They seemed disappointed. They wanted candles.
quotes.speaker: Stephen King
quotes.fake_note: I made this one up — King's documented interview persona is exactly this kind of gruff, self-mocking deflation of the romantic-writer image, and he's said similar things in On Writing and various interviews.
